svg.aria-label: Two ways to give a codebase to a model. On the left, one file that was truncated where the budget ran out, with no index and no way to know it is stale. On the right, a snapshot: parts each under maxPartBytes, a manifest that indexes every file and every skip with its reason, secrets masked rather than emitted, and a validate command that exits 1 when the code has moved.
svg.text: What a plain dump gives you
· one file, cut off where the model's limit ran out
· no index of what was included, or what was left behind
· no record of which revision it came from
· no way to know it drifted after the code moved
· secrets inside normal files travel with it, unless someone looked
You find out something was missing when the answer is wrong.
· parts that each stay under maxPartBytes, never over
· manifest.json: every file and every skip, with the reason
· secrets masked in place — the file stays, the value does not
· a fingerprint, identical on every machine for the same input
· validate: re-hash the repository, exit 1 on drift
You find out something moved before the answer is wrong.
The difference is not speed or format. It is whether the thing you handed over can be checked afterwards.
